newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Xenova still seeks new alliances.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Xenova still seeks new alliances.

text.p: British drug discovery company Xenova Group Plc said on Monday that its alliance with Bristol Myers Squibb Co of the U.S. did not preclude it from seeking other partnerships.
In a telephone interview with Reuters, Xenova chief executive Louis Nisbet said the agreement to cooperate in searching for potential new drugs "still leaves room for other collaborations."
The U.S. company will use its technology to screen Xenova's library of organisms drawn from plants, fungi and bacteria to seek new compounds.

News of the link with Bristol Myers boosted Xenova's share price, which was up 25 pence at 295 in early afternoon trading, although analysts said there was little detail of financial benefits to Xenova in the announcement.

Nisbet said that under its agreement with Bristol Myers, Xenova was not allowed to disclose details of milestone or royalty payments that would flow from the collaboration and any resulting compounds.
He said Bristol Myers would fund the drug discovery programme, and "downstream if they develop a product we get a nice royalty stream."
"It is an extremely attractive formula for a young company like us. We are thrilled we have been able to add a company of this standing to our growing list of partners."
In terms of therapeutic interests, Nisbet said "we can't reveal the specific areas that are involved " but added that "we are working on an area that is important to our collaborator."
Bristol Myers's main areas of therapeutic interest are cardiovascular, metabolic and infectious diseases, central nervous system and dermatological disorders, and cancer.
Nisbet said Xenova would continue with its own drug development programme, which includes a cancer drug which has completed Phase I clinical studies.
Xenova already has a number of partnerships, including research accords with the Parke-Davis arm of Warner Lambert Co and Japan's Suntory Ltd.
